value.behaviour: Restore repairs page data: legacy and malformed input become one default page, elements are restored page by page, and appState's page keys are restored from the supplied data only.
rules: restorePages: a non-array or empty input returns [getDefaultPage()]. Otherwise walk the entries: skip anything that is not an object with a non-empty string `id`, and skip an id already seen (first wins). name is normalizePageName of a string name with fallback getNextPageName(accepted so far). version is a finite number >= 1, else 1. versionNonce and updated are finite numbers, else 0. isDeleted is `!!isDeleted`. Keep tombstones.

restorePages ordering: when every accepted index passes isValidPageIndex and no two are equal, sort live and tombstones together by index then id. Otherwise run assignPageIndices over the accepted records in input order. When no live record remains, return [getDefaultPage()].
restoreActivePageId returns the supplied id when it names a live page, otherwise the first live page's id (FR-21).

restorePageViewports keeps entries whose key names a page in `pages` and whose scrollX, scrollY and zoom are finite, with zoom passed through getNormalizedZoom. Anything else is dropped; a non-object input returns {}.

restoreElementPages returns the input reference when every element's getElementPageId is a page in `pages`, tombstones included. Otherwise it maps: an element on an unknown page, or with no pageId when the default page isn't in the list, becomes a copy on the first live page; a move to DEFAULT_PAGE_ID removes the key. No version bump, like other restore normalization.

restoreElements: run restoreElementPages first when opts.pages is set, so moved elements join the first page's group in array order. When no element has a pageId, call restorePageElements once, so a one-page drawing takes exactly today's path. Otherwise flatMap restorePageElements over groupElementsByPage's groups. One `existingIds` Set is shared across groups, so a duplicate id across pages still gets a new id. Bindings and frames are repaired against one group, which enforces FR-15.

value.behaviour: AppPages owns every change to the page list and the active page: it switches pages, applies remote lists, routes host writes, and replaces the drawing on load.
rules: setActivePage(pageId): return when pageId is the active page or isn't live. No view-mode check here: the role matrix lets view-mode users switch and lets hosts do everything.

setActivePage step 1: call `app.text.textWysiwygSubmitHandler?.()`. Then in flushSync, when state.multiElement or state.selectedLinearElement?.isEditing is set, run `app.actionManager.executeAction(actionFinalize)`, and call `app.setState({})`, so componentDidUpdate commits the Store and the work lands on the leaving page's undo stack (FR-11, FR-17).
setActivePage step 2: call `app.viewport.destroy()`, which only cancels viewport animations and snap-back, so an animation can't move the new page.

setActivePage step 3: read app.state fresh. Build nextState: activePageId; pageViewports with the leaving page's entry set to its {scrollX, scrollY, zoom: zoom.value}; scrollX, scrollY and zoom from the target's entry, or 0, 0 and 1 for a page with none (FR-13); selectedElementIds {}, previousSelectedElementIds {}, selectedGroupIds {}, hoveredElementIds {}, editingGroupId null, selectedLinearElement null, editingTextElement null, newElement null, multiElement null, resizingElement null, selectionElement null, activeEmbeddable null, activeLockedId null, editingFrame null, isCropping false, croppingElementId null, contextMenu null, showHyperlinkPopup false, suggestedBinding null, frameToHighlight null, elementsToHighlight null, snapLines [].

setActivePage step 4: `history.setActivePage(pageId)`. Then in flushSync: `app.scene.setActivePage(pageId)`, `app.store.resetSnapshot(app.scene.getElementsMapIncludingDeleted(), { ...state, ...nextState })`, and `app.setState(nextState)`. Scene and state change in one commit, and nothing is captured, so a switch is not an undo step (FR-17).

setActivePage step 5: call addNewImagesToImageCache() and `app.fonts.loadSceneFonts(state.currentItemFontFamily).then((fontFaces) => app.fonts.onLoaded(fontFaces))`, because both only walk the active page.
createPage({ name, activate = true } = {}): build with newPage, commit `pages: [...state.pages, page]` in flushSync, call setActivePage when activate, and return the record.
renamePage and movePage call the pure functions and commit in flushSync when the list reference changed.

deletePage returns false when the page isn't live or is the last live page (FR-10). When it is the active page, setActivePage(getNeighbourPageId(live, pageId)) first. Then map app.scene.getPageElements(pageId) with newElementWith(element, { isDeleted: true }) for non-deleted elements, and write with `app.scene.replaceElementsByPage(new Map([[pageId, elements]]))`. Call history.deletePage(pageId). Commit the list from the pure deletePage and pageViewports without that key in flushSync. Return true.

applyPages(pages): return when `pages === state.pages`. Compute the ids live in `pages`. Call history.deletePage for each previously live id no longer live. Commit `pages` and pageViewports pruned to live ids in flushSync. When the active page is no longer live, setActivePage(getNeighbourPageId(prevLive, activePageId, nextIds) ?? first live id) (FR-27).

routeElements(elements, wholeDrawing): when not wholeDrawing and one live page and `!app.scene.hasOtherPages()`, return null, which is the constant-time path to replaceAllElements. When wholeDrawing, return groupElementsByPage(elements) with an empty group added for the active page if it has none. Otherwise, for each element: a pageId naming a live page goes there; else an id found in arrayToMap(app.scene.getAllElementsIncludingDeleted()) goes to that element's page; else the active page (FR-16). When elements is empty, return a Map with an empty group for the active page.
isUndoableReplace(pages): true when the scene has no other pages, the current live list is one page with DEFAULT_PAGE_ID, and getLivePages(pages) is one page with DEFAULT_PAGE_ID.

replaceDrawing(elements, appState): when isUndoableReplace(appState.pages), call app.scene.replaceAllElements(elements) and return. Otherwise call history.clear() and history.setActivePage(appState.activePageId), then app.scene.replaceElementsByPage(groupElementsByPage(elements), { replaceAll: true, activePageId: appState.activePageId }), then app.store.resetSnapshot(app.scene.getElementsMapIncludingDeleted(), { ...app.state, ...appState }).
omitPageState returns a copy of appState without pages, activePageId and pageViewports, and returns null for null.

value.behaviour: The tab bar: lists live pages, switches on click, and in edit mode creates, renames, reorders and deletes.
rules: The file imports "./PageTabs.scss". Props are { app: AppClassProperties; appState: UIAppState }. Pages come from getLivePages(appState.pages). All changes go through app.pages. Editing controls (add button, menu buttons, rename, drag) render only when !appState.viewModeEnabled (FR-12).

Markup: root div class `page-tabs`, data-testid `page-tabs`, data-viewport-ui `bottom`. Inside, a div role=tablist with aria-label t("pages.tabList"), class `page-tabs__list`, which scrolls when tabs overflow (FR-6). Each page is a div role=presentation class `page-tabs__tab` (with `page-tabs__tab--active`) holding a button role=tab, aria-selected, tabIndex 0 on the active tab and -1 otherwise, title the page name, data-testid `page-tab-${id}`, and in edit mode a button aria-label t("pages.options"), aria-haspopup menu, data-testid `page-tab-menu-${id}`, tabIndex 0 on the active tab and -1 otherwise. After the list, the add button with aria-label t("pages.add"), data-testid `page-tab-add`, PlusIcon.

A tab's click calls app.pages.setActivePage(id), then app.focusContainer() when event.detail > 0, so a pointer click gives the keyboard back to the canvas but keyboard activation keeps focus on the tab.
A useEffect on activePageId calls `scrollIntoView?.({ block: "nearest", inline: "nearest" })` on the active tab; the optional call is for jsdom.

Keyboard on a tab: ArrowRight and ArrowLeft move focus to the next and previous tab, wrapping; Home and End to the first and last; F2 starts rename in edit mode. Handled keys call preventDefault and stopPropagation so canvas shortcuts don't fire (NFR-5). Enter and Space are the button's own click.

Rename: double-click or the menu's rename replaces the tab button with an input, aria-label t("pages.renameLabel"), data-testid `page-tab-rename-input`, autofocused and selected, maxLength MAX_PAGE_NAME_LENGTH. Enter or blur commits with app.pages.renamePage. Escape cancels: a ref marks it so the blur that follows doesn't commit. Keys in the input stop propagation. After either, focus returns to the tab (FR-8).

Reorder: in edit mode the tab div is draggable. onDragStart stores the id in a ref and calls `event.dataTransfer?.setData("text/plain", id)`; onDragOver calls preventDefault; onDrop calls app.pages.movePage(draggedId, position of the target tab) and stopPropagation (FR-9). Drag state lives in the ref, not dataTransfer, so jsdom's fireEvent works without one.

Menu: one menu at a time, in state as the page id. A div role=menu class `page-tabs__menu`, rendered as a child of the root with `left` from the trigger's offset, opening above the bar. Items are buttons role=menuitem with data-testids `page-menu-rename`, `page-menu-move-left`, `page-menu-move-right`, `page-menu-delete`, labelled with t("pages.rename"), t("pages.moveLeft"), t("pages.moveRight"), t("pages.delete"). Move left is disabled at position 0, move right at the last position, delete when one page remains. The first item takes focus on open. useOutsideClick and Escape close it and return focus to the trigger.

Delete: when app.scene.getPageElements(id) has a non-deleted element, open ConfirmDialog with title t("pages.deleteConfirmTitle") and body t("pages.deleteConfirm", { name }), and call app.pages.deletePage on confirm. An empty page deletes at once (FR-10).
Add calls app.pages.createPage().
